candidateEvaluations.label: Fold bias+scale into one addcmul against cached constant operands, cutting the hot path from 4 kernels to 3
candidateEvaluations.title: Fold bias+scale into one addcmul against cached constant operands, cutting the hot path from 4 kernels to 3
candidateEvaluations.hypothesis: The hot path is launch-bound, so removing one of round-1's four serialized elementwise kernels should cut roughly one kernel's worth of launch+execution (~2us) from p50, while keeping the same math order for the multiply coefficients (1.25 and 0.75 stay exact; only the association of the -0.125 bias moves to the front).
candidateEvaluations.change: run(inputs) now does: out = torch.addcmul(bias, x, ones, value=1.25) -> out.add_(y, alpha=0.75) -> return torch.relu_(out). 'ones' and 'bias' are constant full-shape buffers (1.0 and -0.125) memoized per (shape, dtype, device); they contain no input data and are never written, so no result or input caching is involved. No .clone(), no intermediate temporary, and neither input is mutated.
